content.text:
I wrote `src/markdown.js` from scratch because the GitHub search turned up nothing worth reusing. The one public smoke test passes (`node --test`: 1 pass, 0 fail). I haven't run the larger hidden suite.

I did the one GitHub search through the browser. It returned only a 2017 mini-parser with no stated license, a PHP project and an unrelated config repo, and none of them targets CommonMark output. I recorded this in `PROVENANCE.json`, which is `[]`-equivalent: no code was reused, so there is no `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

`render(markdown)` covers the whole SPEC subset: ATX headings, paragraphs, emphasis, inline code, links and images, single-level lists, fenced code, blockquotes and thematic breaks. It escapes `& < > "` and never passes raw HTML through. I also added setext headings, backslash escapes and hard line breaks, which the SPEC doesn't require.

I spot-checked some inputs by eye, including `***a***`, `snake_case` and a fenced block with `<a>&`. I did not compare output against commonmark.js. A link whose URL contains a space is not turned into a link; it comes out as plain text.
